text:
Candidate sampling can reverse model comparisons, so diagnostic stability across candidate sets cannot be assumed. RecSys 2025’s [On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examines sampling resolution, agreement with full evaluation, robustness to exposure bias, and predictive power. Earlier [sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establishes that sampled rankings can disagree with full-catalog rankings even in expectation. [Subbiah et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371) demonstrate benefits from correcting sampled rank estimates during training; this does not establish interchangeability between candidate protocols.

Representation collapse provides a complementary diagnostic axis. [Guo et al., ICML 2024](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html) identify embeddings occupying low-dimensional subspaces as a limitation on recommendation-model scaling. The [SpecFormer preprint (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24025) connects recommendation embedding and attention collapse with concentrated singular spectra. These findings motivate spectral measurements alongside mean cosine; neither establishes that increasing effective rank necessarily improves this benchmark’s HR@10.

Suggested audit, inferred from these findings: fix users and training-prefix targets; compare equal-sized, unique uniform, popularity-matched, and title/description-similar candidate sets against full-catalog ranks. Report centered effective rank with its spectral normalization explicitly defined, embedding norms, cosine distributions, catalog coverage, and recommendation concentration. Calibrate responses using positive global score scaling, which preserves rankings, plus progressively truncated representations and injected noise, whose ranking effects must be measured. Use paired user bootstrap intervals, stratified by category, and repeated candidate draws to distinguish user uncertainty from sampler variability. Treat these as explanatory diagnostics; retain pinned macro validation HR@10 as the sole selection objective.
